name: Helm: install & upgrade a release
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture (package management). Helm installs a chart as a named release and tracks revisions; values (via --set or a values file) parameterize the manifests. Install a release with a custom value, then upgrade it to change that value. Graded on the Kubernetes objects Helm renders.

questions.title: Install a Helm release
questions.teach:
`helm install <release> <chart>` renders a chart's templates with its **values** and applies them as a tracked **release**. `--set key=value` overrides a value on the fly; `-n <ns>` targets a namespace. `helm create <name>` scaffolds a ready-to-install chart (a Deployment+Service whose replica count comes from `replicaCount`).

**Gotcha:** Helm labels everything it manages with `app.kubernetes.io/instance: <release>` and `managed-by: Helm` — that's how you (and graders) find a release's objects. The release name is namespaced-unique.
questions.prompt:
Using Helm, install a release named `web` into namespace `helm-learn` with **2 replicas** (`replicaCount=2`). Scaffold a chart with `helm create <name>` if you need one.

Target: a Helm-managed Deployment (label `app.kubernetes.io/instance=web`) exists in `helm-learn` with `spec.replicas = 2`.
questions.hint: `helm create app` then `helm install web ./app -n helm-learn --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2`. Verify: `helm -n helm-learn list` and `kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web`.
questions.solution:
helm create app
helm install web ./app -n helm-learn --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2
helm -n helm-learn list
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web

verification.description: Helm release web installed in helm-learn with 2 replicas

questions.eli5:
Imagine you want to bake a cake, but instead of measuring flour and eggs every time, someone hands you a **cake mix box**. That box is a Helm **chart**: a reusable kit of Kubernetes recipes (Deployments, Services, etc.) with blanks you can fill in.

**Helm** is the baker. `helm install web ./app` means: *"Take this cake-mix box (`./app`), bake one cake, and call this particular cake `web`."* That named cake is a **release** — Helm remembers it so you can tweak or throw it away later as one unit, instead of hunting down every individual object.

The box has default settings written on it (in a file called `values.yaml`). `--set replicaCount=2` is you scribbling over one of those defaults right before baking: *"actually, make 2 of these, not 1."* That number flows into the recipe and comes out as a Deployment with 2 replicas.

`helm create app` just gives you a fresh, ready-to-bake sample box to practice with.

**Watch out for:**

- **The namespace must exist**, or use `--create-namespace` (as in the hint) — otherwise the install fails.
- **Release names are unique per namespace.** Try to `install web` twice in the same namespace and Helm refuses ("cannot re-use a name"). Two different namespaces *can* each have a `web`.
- **`--set` keys must match the chart's real values.** A typo like `replicaCont=2` doesn't error loudly — it's just quietly ignored, and you get the default.
- **Helm stamps every object** it makes with labels `app.kubernetes.io/instance=web` and `managed-by=Helm`. That's how you (and the grader) find a release's pieces — look for those labels.
- **Don't hand-edit Helm's objects** with `kubectl edit`; Helm won't know, and your change gets wiped on the next upgrade.
questions.deepDive:
## Helm install — full rundown

### Mental model
Helm is the **package manager for Kubernetes**. A **chart** is a package: templated manifests plus a `values.yaml` of defaults. `helm install` **renders** those templates with the merged values and applies the result to the cluster as a single tracked unit called a **release**. Helm stores release state (rendered manifests, values, revision history) as Secrets in the release's namespace — so you manage many objects as one thing.

Helm 3 is **client-only** (no Tiller). It talks to the API server using your kubeconfig, just like `kubectl`.

### Chart layout (`helm create app`)
```
app/
├── Chart.yaml          # name, version, appVersion
├── values.yaml         # DEFAULT values (replicaCount, image, service, ...)
├── templates/
│   ├── deployment.yaml # uses {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
│   ├── service.yaml
│   ├── _helpers.tpl    # named template helpers (labels, names)
│   └── ...
└── charts/             # subchart dependencies
```
The scaffolded chart's Deployment replica count comes straight from `.Values.replicaCount` (default `1`).

### The install command
```bash
helm install web ./app -n helm-learn --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2
#            └name┘ └chart┘ └─namespace─┘ └ make ns if absent ┘ └ value override ┘
```
| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `web` | release name (unique within the namespace) |
| `./app` | chart source (local dir, `.tgz`, or `repo/chart`) |
| `-n helm-learn` | target namespace |
| `--create-namespace` | create the ns if it doesn't exist |
| `--set replicaCount=2` | override one value inline |

### Ways to supply values (precedence: later wins)
| Method | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| chart default | `values.yaml` | baseline |
| values file | `-f my-values.yaml` | can repeat; merged in order |
| `--set` | `--set replicaCount=2` | scalar/override; `--set a.b=c` for nesting |
| `--set-string` | `--set-string tag=1.0` | forces string (avoid `1.0`→number) |
| `--set-file` | `--set-file cert=./tls.crt` | value from a file |

Precedence, lowest→highest: `values.yaml` < `-f` files (in order) < `--set`.

### Verify / inspect
```bash
helm -n helm-learn list                       # or: helm list -A
helm -n helm-learn status web
helm -n helm-learn get values web             # effective user-set values
helm -n helm-learn get manifest web           # exact rendered YAML
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.replicas}'; echo   # -> 2
```

### Preview without installing
```bash
helm template web ./app --set replicaCount=2         # render locally, no cluster
helm install web ./app -n helm-learn --dry-run --debug --set replicaCount=2
```

### The standard Helm labels (how graders find objects)
The default chart stamps every object via `_helpers.tpl`:
| Label | Value |
|---|---|
| `app.kubernetes.io/instance` | `web` (the release name) |
| `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` | `Helm` |
| `app.kubernetes.io/name` | the chart name |
Select with `-l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web` to scope to one release.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Namespace doesn't exist** → install fails unless you pass `--create-namespace` (or precreate it).
- **Duplicate release name in a namespace** → `cannot re-use a name that is still in use`. Names are unique **per namespace**, not globally.
- **Typo in a `--set` key** is silently ignored (chart just uses the default) — verify replicas actually changed.
- **`--set` number vs string**: `--set tag=1.0` becomes the float `1`; use `--set-string tag=1.0` for versions.
- **Nested values** use dots: `--set image.tag=1.21`, and commas separate multiple: `--set a=1,b=2`.
- **Don't `kubectl edit`** Helm-managed objects — Helm's stored manifest won't match and the change is lost on `helm upgrade`.
- **`helm install` is not idempotent** — to re-run safely use `helm upgrade --install`.

### Quick reference
```bash
helm create app
helm install web ./app -n helm-learn --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2
helm -n helm-learn list
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web   # replicas = 2
```

questions.title: Upgrade the release (change a value)
questions.teach:
`helm upgrade <release> <chart> --set key=value` applies a new revision with changed values; `helm rollback <release> <rev>` returns to a prior one. Each upgrade bumps the release **revision**.

**Gotcha:** `helm upgrade` needs the chart again (same `./app` or repo ref) — it's not `kubectl edit`. Use `--reuse-values` to keep previously-set overrides you're not changing.
questions.prompt:
Upgrade the `web` release to **3 replicas** (`replicaCount=3`), keeping it a Helm upgrade (new revision).

Target: the `web` Deployment in `helm-learn` now has `spec.replicas = 3`.
questions.hint: `helm upgrade web ./app -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3`. Check the bump: `helm -n helm-learn history web` and `kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web`.
questions.solution:
helm upgrade web ./app -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3
helm -n helm-learn history web
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.replicas}'; echo
questions.eli5:
You baked your cake (`web`) with 2 layers. Now you want 3 layers. You don't throw the cake away and start over — you tell the baker: *"same box, same cake, but this time make it 3."* That's **`helm upgrade`**.

`helm upgrade web ./app --set replicaCount=3` re-bakes the `web` release from the chart with the new value, and the Deployment goes from 2 replicas to 3. Crucially, Helm keeps a **logbook**: every install and upgrade is a numbered **revision** (1, 2, 3...). So you can always flip back to how things were with `helm rollback web 1`, like an "undo" button.

The thing people forget: `helm upgrade` is **not** `kubectl edit`. You must hand Helm the **chart again** (`./app`), because Helm re-renders the whole package from scratch — it's not poking one field, it's regenerating everything from the recipe + values.

**Watch out for:**

- **You must pass the chart again** (`./app` or the repo reference). Leaving it out fails — upgrade isn't an in-place field edit.
- **`--set` only changes what you name; unnamed values reset to the chart defaults** on each upgrade. If you set several values at install time and only `--set` one now, the others revert. Use **`--reuse-values`** to carry forward your earlier overrides (or re-pass them all).
- **Each upgrade bumps the revision number.** Check it with `helm history web` — handy for confirming the upgrade actually happened and for rollbacks.
- **Rollback also makes a new revision.** Rolling back from rev 3 to rev 1 creates rev 4 that looks like rev 1 — it doesn't erase history.
- **Don't hand-edit with `kubectl`** between upgrades; Helm will overwrite your change because it re-renders from the chart.
questions.deepDive:
## Helm upgrade & rollback — full rundown

### Mental model
`helm upgrade` creates a **new revision** of an existing release by re-rendering the chart with (possibly) new values and reconciling the result against what's in the cluster. It is **not** an in-place edit of one field — Helm regenerates the full manifest set from the chart + merged values, diffs against the last release, and applies the change. Every install/upgrade/rollback increments the release **revision**; Helm keeps the history so you can roll back.

### The upgrade command
```bash
helm upgrade web ./app -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3
#            └name┘ └chart┘ └─namespace─┘ └ new value ┘
```
You must supply the **chart again** (`./app`, a `.tgz`, or `repo/chart`) — upgrade re-renders from it. Omitting the chart is an error.

### Values on upgrade: the critical behavior
By default, `helm upgrade` computes values as **chart defaults + the flags you pass THIS time**. Values you `--set` during a *previous* install are **NOT** automatically carried forward.

| Flag | Effect on values |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | chart `values.yaml` defaults + this call's `-f`/`--set` only |
| `--reuse-values` | start from the **last release's** computed values, apply this call's overrides |
| `--reset-values` | discard prior overrides, use chart defaults + this call's flags (the default-ish behavior, made explicit) |
| `--reset-then-reuse-values` | reset to chart defaults, then merge last release's values, then this call's |

So if install used `--set image.tag=1.21 --set replicaCount=2` and you later run `helm upgrade web ./app --set replicaCount=3`, the `image.tag` reverts to the chart default unless you add `--reuse-values` or re-pass it.

### Idempotent install-or-upgrade
```bash
helm upgrade --install web ./app -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3
# installs if 'web' doesn't exist, upgrades if it does — great for scripts/CI
```

### Revisions, history, rollback
```bash
helm -n helm-learn history web            # table of revisions + status + description
helm -n helm-learn get values web         # user-supplied values of current revision
helm -n helm-learn get values web --revision 2
helm -n helm-learn rollback web 1         # revert to revision 1 (creates a NEW revision)
helm -n helm-learn rollback web           # roll back to the immediately previous revision
```
Example history after install (rev1=2 replicas) then upgrade (rev2=3 replicas):
| REVISION | STATUS | DESCRIPTION |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | superseded | Install complete |
| 2 | deployed | Upgrade complete |

**Rollback makes a new revision.** Rolling from rev 2 back to rev 1 produces rev 3 whose content equals rev 1 — history is append-only.

### Useful flags
| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--set k=v` | override value inline (dots nest, commas separate) |
| `-f file.yaml` | values file override |
| `--reuse-values` | keep previous overrides you aren't changing |
| `--atomic` | roll back automatically if the upgrade fails |
| `--wait` | block until resources are ready |
| `--timeout 5m` | how long to wait with `--wait`/`--atomic` |
| `--dry-run --debug` | preview the rendered change without applying |
| `--install` | install if the release is absent |

### Verify the result
```bash
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.replicas}'; echo    # -> 3
helm -n helm-learn status web
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Upgrade is not `kubectl edit`.** You must pass the chart; it re-renders everything. Manual `kubectl` edits get overwritten on the next upgrade.
- **Previous `--set` overrides are dropped** unless you use `--reuse-values` (or re-pass them). Classic surprise: an unrelated value "resets" after upgrade.
- **Typo'd `--set` key** is silently ignored — confirm the replica count actually changed via `helm history`/`kubectl get`.
- **Each upgrade bumps the revision**; a no-op upgrade can still create a revision. Use `helm history` to confirm.
- **Rollback creates a new revision**, it doesn't delete history; the target revision number must exist in `helm history`.
- **`--atomic`** auto-rolls-back on failure — handy, but it also deletes newly-added resources if the upgrade fails.

### Quick reference
```bash
helm upgrade web ./app -n helm-learn --set replicaCount=3
helm -n helm-learn history web                                    # see revision bump
kubectl -n helm-learn get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=web \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.replicas}'; echo                   # 3
# undo:
helm -n helm-learn rollback web 1
```
